title: Expiry TTL: an expired approval cannot be approved or silently executed
risk: A month-old approval is reused to release a campaign whose prices, consent and inventory have all changed, executing a commitment nobody currently endorses.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
APV-T2-CAMP carries expires_at 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z, exactly the frozen clock.

steps.action: Approve one second before the expiry instant using the injected clock
steps.expected: HTTP 200 with status APPROVED; the item is released once.

steps.action: Attempt to approve a second item after its expiry instant has passed
steps.expected: The decision is refused with an expired status response; the item moves to an expired terminal state rather than executing.

steps.action: Advance the clock further and inspect the queue
steps.expected: The expired item is no longer actionable and no automatic execution has occurred for it.

assertions: The expiry boundary is evaluated against server time; at exactly expires_at the item is no longer approvable.
An expired approval never executes, and expiry is terminal rather than silently renewed.
The expired item's terminal state is recorded in the audit trail with the expiry instant used.
Expiry does not delete the reviewed payload, so the audit trail remains complete.
forbidden: Extending the TTL automatically when an operator opens the item.
Falling back to execution when the expiry check errors.
Treating an expired item as cancelled and releasing its reservations without recording why.
evidence: Decision responses before and after expiry with the evaluated instants.
Approval record terminal states and audit rows.
cleanup: Delete gov- approval rows after exporting the expiry audit evidence.
automation: Time is injected at the approval service boundary so the boundary is exact; the service itself, not the test, decides approvability.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
